prompts.title: Classic Monochrome Portrait of Elegant Gentleman
prompts.prompt:
Create an ultra-realistic black-and-white luxury men’s fashion portrait of the uploaded person, preserving their natural facial identity, hairstyle, skin texture, existing facial hair, physique, and shoulder width.
Use a vertical 4:5 waste-up composition photographed from sufficient distance. Leave approximately 10% clear headroom and generous negative space on both sides. Keep the complete suit jacket and upper trousers visible, with the subject’s silhouette occupying only 50–60% of the frame width.
Create the body angle sequentially: first rotate the entire torso approximately 15–20° toward the left edge of the final image, then turn only the head gently back toward the camera. The shoulder on the right side of the final image must sit visibly nearer to the lens, while the shoulder on the left appears slightly smaller, lower, and farther away. Keep the shoulders diagonal to the image plane—never parallel, squared, or symmetrical. Maintain direct eye contact, a subtly lowered chin, and a calm, serious expression.
Position the camera at upper-chest height with an almost level optical axis and a barely perceptible upward perspective. Use an 85mm portrait lens from approximately 3 metres away to preserve a slender torso and natural facial and shoulder proportions.
Dress the subject in a tailored deep-black double-breasted suit with natural structured shoulders, peak lapels, six dark buttons, a crisp white shirt with only the top button open, a small monochrome paisley pocket square, and a silver chronograph watch with a dark dial.
Place the left forearm across the upper abdomen from the right side of the frame toward the left, displaying the watch near the centre of the torso. Position the right hand directly below, gently adjusting the left cuff. Keep the elbows close and the hand arrangement compact.
Place the subject against a continuous seamless matte-black studio cyclorama with a smooth, non-reflective finish. Keep the backdrop completely clean and featureless, with no texture, marble, patterns, seams, wall edges, floor horizon, props, or visible light source. Allow only a subtle charcoal-black tonal falloff behind the subject while maintaining a predominantly deep-black background.
Use controlled low-key studio lighting with a large gridded softbox positioned approximately 45° above and to the left side of the final frame. Illuminate the left side of the forehead, cheekbone, nose, hair, suit, hands, and watch while allowing the right side to fall into deep but detailed shadow. Add minimal frontal fill to preserve natural facial and suit detail, plus a very subtle flagged edge light from rear-right to define the shadow-side hair and shoulder against the black backdrop without creating a visible halo.
Maintain restrained exposure and smooth highlight roll-off on the face, white shirt, hands, and watch. Preserve detail in the black suit through controlled tonal separation rather than bright lighting. Keep the subject naturally integrated with the dark studio environment while retaining clear but soft-edged separation from the backdrop.
Use gray scale, controlled silver-grey highlights, natural skin texture, realistic suit fabric, low-key exposure, and cinematic chiaroscuro. Avoid tight framing, enlarged shoulders, frontal symmetry, flat lighting, over-bright skin, crushed suit detail, harsh rim light, background hotspots, visible gradients, text, logos, or graphics.

prompts.title: Monochrome Headphone Profile
prompts.prompt:
Use the uploaded image only for face and identity reference. Preserve the person’s natural facial features and overall identity with high accuracy.

Create an ultra-realistic, high-contrast, black-and-white, low-key studio portrait of the reference subject in a quiet moment of musical immersion.

Composition & Framing
Use a vertical 4:5 aspect ratio. Show the subject in a strict 90-degree right-facing side profile, framed as a lower-chest-up / mid-torso portrait. Keep the subject centered overall, but make him appear smaller in frame, as if photographed from a little farther away.

Leave generous negative space above the head, clearly more headroom than in a typical tight portrait. Also keep moderate open space in front of the face on the right. Make sure the full hair shape, headphones, hood, shoulder, and upper torso are comfortably visible. Do not crop too close.
Pose & Expression
Keep the head in a clean right-facing profile with the chin slightly raised. Eyes gently closed, brow completely relaxed, lips softly and naturally rested together, jaw loose, and facial muscles calm. The expression should feel quiet, immersed, serene, and meditative, not pouty, tense, dramatic, or fashion-posed.

Wardrobe & Headphones
The subject wears premium over-ear wireless headphones with a smooth wide headband, thick matte ear cushions, and large circular metallic ear cups with a clear brushed / spun metal texture.

He wears a white hoodie. The hoodie should look smooth, plain, soft, and clean, with no visible fabric texture. Avoid rough weave or strong cloth grain. The hood rests naturally around the upper back and neck, creating a thick layered collar, with one flat drawstring hanging naturally down the chest.
Lighting
Use dramatic low-key chiaroscuro studio lighting that closely matches the original image.

The main light is a strong hard rim light placed behind and slightly above the subject on the right side. This rim light should create a crisp silver outline along:

the outer hair silhouette

the forehead, nose bridge, lips, and chin edge

the outer metallic edge of the headphone cup

the hoodie collar, shoulder ridge, and upper sleeve
Add only a very weak, highly diffused front-left fill light so the face and hoodie remain visible without becoming flat or bright. The fill should be extremely subtle. Keep the shadows deep and moody. The face should not look evenly lit or front-lit. The original image’s lighting should feel more like a sculpted edge-lit portrait than a standard soft studio portrait.

Background
Use a pure seamless black background with no visible texture, no environment, and no extra elements.

Camera & Detail
Simulate a portrait telephoto lens (85mm–105mm) with f/5.6 to f/8 depth of field so the entire subject stays sharp — including hair texture, skin detail, headphones, hoodie shape, and drawstring. Keep the image crisp and realistic, but do not over-emphasize fabric texture.

Important Constraints
Keep more negative space above the head
Make the subject appear farther from the camera
Keep the subject centered overall
Chin slightly raised
Expression must be soft, calm, and meditative
Lighting must stay dark, sculpted, and rim-light dominant
Do not make the face too bright or too evenly lit
Hoodie must remain smooth and plain without any texture
Do not make it a tight crop
Do not rotate the face toward the camera
Do not add text, logos, watermark, or extra objects

prompts.title: Family Sequence
prompts.prompt:
Create a classic low-key black-and-white studio portrait of a family of four arranged in a staggered side-profile composition, all facing right. Maintain accurate identity and face matching to the provided reference image for all four subjects — preserve exact facial structure, proportions, skin texture, hairlines.
Mid-chest shot (cropped from mid chest upward), tight vertical composition. All four subjects are wearing solid matte black t-shirts with no logos, no reflective elements — blending subtly into shadow while maintaining garment structure.
Diagonal alignment from front-left (father closest to camera) to back-right (youngest child farthest). Overlapping layered composition.
CRITICAL — Natural Height-Based Staggered Arrangement:

Subjects must be arranged in realistic descending height order consistent with a natural family hierarchy. The father (foreground) is the tallest, followed slightly behind by the mother, who is slightly shorter. Behind her stands the first child, clearly shorter than the mother, and, in the far background, the second child, the shortest of all. The top of each subject’s head forms a gradual downward diagonal slope from left (tallest father) to right (shortest child). Eye levels must also progressively lower in the same sequence. This height progression must appear anatomically natural and realistic, not artificially aligned or equalized. Maintain accurate proportional scaling and perspective depth consistent with real-world height differences.
True monochrome (black and white), high contrast, deep blacks, smooth midtone transitions. Dramatic chiaroscuro lighting with a single directional key light from camera-right, slightly above eye level, no equipment/object visible in frame. Strong shadow falloff into pure black background. Deep negative space on the left.
Sharp catchlights in all eyes from a small gridded softbox. Crisp highlight definition on nose bridges, cheekbones, lips, and jawlines.
Father (foreground, sharpest focus): His expression appears steady and confident with a subtle smile. His gaze is fixed forward, conveying strength and leadership. Visible individual hairs, strong skin micro-contrast, wear a black t-shirt fading into shadow.
Mother (second): She has a soft, graceful smile (upper teeth visible). Long voluminous wavy hair, subtle earrings, smooth skin, and wear a black outfit.
Child (third): Her expression shows youthful curiosity and positivity, with a subtle smile (upper teeth visible), slightly pulled-back natural hair, and a simple black outfit.
Child (background): He looks calm and thoughtful. His face carries innocence and quiet confidence, as if observing something meaningful ahead.
Lens look: 85mm–135mm telephoto compression, no distortion.

Aperture look: f/5.6–f/8 layered depth, foreground sharpest with subtle gradual falloff.
Ultra-detailed skin texture, realistic pores, cinematic tonal grading, professional studio photography, timeless, museum-quality.
4K resolution detail, ultra-sharp, high micro-contrast, refined tonal range.

prompts.title: Chiaroscuro
prompts.prompt:
Create a hyper-realistic, high-contrast black-and-white low-key studio portrait of a young woman in a tight vertical composition. Use a three-quarter side profile view, with her head tilted slightly upward (about 20–30 degrees) toward an unseen light source above and in front of her. Her expression must feel calm, introspective, and contemplative.
Lighting (Critical):

Use a single hard directional key light positioned above and slightly to the front-left. This creates dramatic chiaroscuro lighting with strong highlights along the forehead, nose bridge, lips, and chin, while the opposite side of the face, neck, and background fall into deep pure black shadow. Maintain extreme tonal contrast with clean highlight separation and crushed blacks.
Skin and Micro-Detail:

Render ultra-detailed, natural skin texture with visible pores, fine vellus hairs (peach fuzz), and realistic tonal transitions. Preserve authentic epidermal detail without smoothing or beautification. Skin must appear natural, not plastic.
Eyes and Lips:

The visible eye must be razor sharp with clear iris detail and a realistic catchlight reflection matching the light source. Eyelashes must be individually defined. Lips should be slightly parted with natural texture, fine lines, and soft realistic highlights.
Hair and Focus:

Hair near the face must show individual strands with sharp detail. Hair and neck farther from the focal plane should gradually fall into soft blur, creating shallow depth of field.
Lens and Technical Characteristics:

Simulate an 85mm or 105mm macro portrait lens. Maintain natural facial proportions with no distortion. Use shallow depth of field with sharp focus on the eye, nose bridge, cheek, and lips.
Background:

Pure black seamless background with no visible texture or objects.
Style and Quality:

Low-key photography, monochrome fine art portrait, dramatic studio lighting, cinematic chiaroscuro, hyper-realistic detail, professional editorial photography, 8K resolution, 2:3 aspect ratio, ultra-sharp focus, clean tonal range.

prompts.title: Amber Circular Spotlight on Face
prompts.prompt:
Use the uploaded image ONLY for identity reference. Preserve the natural face shape, facial proportions, forehead, eyebrows, eye shape and spacing, nose, lips, jawline, skin tone, and natural facial asymmetry with high accuracy. Do not beautify, reshape, age-change, or blend the face with another identity. The person must remain clearly recognizable even with closed eyes and warm lighting.

Create an ultra-realistic, warm cinematic studio portrait of the uploaded woman standing directly in front of a dark wall.

Composition and Framing:
Use a vertical 4:5 aspect ratio. Frame the subject from the lower torso to the head, showing the full head, neck, shoulders, upper arms, and most of the black T-shirt. Keep her centered and front-facing or slightly off-camera facing, with generous headroom and balanced negative space on both sides. Do not crop the head or shoulders.

Pose:
She stands upright with her upper back and shoulders resting lightly against the wall. Her body and face are aligned toward the camera, shoulders naturally lowered, arms relaxed beside her body and continuing beyond the lower edge of the frame.

Face, Hair, and Expression:
Her eyes are gently closed, and chin slightly raised, creating a calm, soft natural expression. Keep the facial muscles natural and relaxed. Style her natural color hair in a loose, side-parted low bun, with a few natural wispy strands around the ear, cheek, and neck.

Outfit:
A plain matte-black short-sleeve crew-neck T-shirt with realistic cotton texture and subtle natural folds. No jewelry, graphics, logos, or accessories.

Lighting:
Use one strong, warm golden-amber directional spotlight positioned in front of the subject on camera-left and slightly above face level. The light directly illuminates the face, neck, collarbones, and upper shoulders while producing natural warm highlights and soft facial shadow transitions.

Aim the same spotlight toward the wall to create a large, perfectly round golden-orange pool of light centered behind the subject’s head and upper torso. The circle must be much larger than her head, with its upper edge well above her hair and its lower portion extending behind her shoulders and torso. Give it a clearly visible but slightly feathered circular boundary, an evenly glowing golden center, and a gradual amber falloff. It should look like a real spotlight projected onto the wall, not a glowing ring or digital halo.

Because the subject is standing close to the wall, create a dark, sharply defined silhouette of her head, neck, and shoulders offset toward the viewer’s right. Keep the shadow direction fully consistent with the front-left light source. Allow the lower face, arms, and black T-shirt to gradually fall into deep shadow.

Background:
A clean, smooth, matte dark chocolate-brown studio wall. Outside the circular spotlight, the wall transitions into deep brown-black shadows with a natural vignette. No visible floor, wall seams, props, smoke, or additional background elements.

Camera and Finish:
Eye-level camera, straight-on angle, 50mm lens, approximately f/4. Keep the face sharply detailed while retaining clearly visible halo edges and wall shadow. Warm tungsten color temperature, rich amber-brown cinematic grading, strong chiaroscuro contrast, natural skin pores and texture, natural highlight roll-off, editorial photography quality, high resolution.

Avoid front fill light, backlight, rim light, cool tones, excessive blur, artificial skin smoothing, plastic facial texture, composited appearance, text, icons, and watermarks.
